record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Fix k ≥ 2. In the Even Number Game G_k, Player 1 chooses a set A of k natural numbers none of which she has played before, then Player 2 chooses an even number between min(A) and max(A), inclusive, that he has not played before; Player II loses when he has no legal move. It is known that Player 1 wins for k = 2 and k = 3. For k ≥ 4, does Player 1 have a winning strategy in G_k?

evidence.quote: Given a natural number k ≥ 2, the game Gk is a game with two players who take turns to play natural numbers. Player 1 plays a set A of k integers ... then Player 2 plays an even number between min(A) and max(A) ... Player II loses when he has no legal moves.
It was shown in [1] that for k = 2, 3, Player 1 has a winning strategy in the game Gk. For k ≥ 4, this is unknown. Problem 4. For k ≥ 4, does Player 1 have a winning strategy in the game Gk?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer k ≥ 2. Define the two-player game G_k played on the natural numbers as follows. Players alternate moves, with Player 1 moving first. On each of her turns, Player 1 selects a set A ⊆ ℕ of exactly k natural numbers, none of which she has chosen on any previous turn (the elements of A must all be new for Player 1, but may have been used by Player 2). On each of his turns following Player 1's move, Player 2 selects a single even natural number n with min(A) ≤ n ≤ max(A) such that n has not been chosen by Player 2 on any previous turn. Player 2 loses if at some point he has no legal move; otherwise the play continues indefinitely and Player 2 wins.

It is known that Player 1 has a winning strategy in G_2 and in G_3. For every k ≥ 4, does Player 1 have a winning strategy in G_k?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a 2025 collection of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory; the cases k = 2, 3 are known to be wins for Player 1, while k ≥ 4 is stated as unknown. No published resolution was located in a brief web search.
